cards.title: Accops HyID (Silver/Gold/Platinum) vs Cisco Duo Editions (Free, MFA, Access, Beyond): Feature Checklist Spreadsheet (2021)
cards.key_problem: A prospect pricing Cisco Duo per edition needs to see which Duo tier a given HyID edition matches, and where Duo needs an extra gateway or cloud sync that HyID does on-premise.
key_outcomes: One-sheet x/no checklist: four Duo editions with their list prices of the time (Free up to 10 users, MFA, Access, Beyond - USD 3/6/9 per user per month) against HyID Silver, Gold and Platinum

Sections: user trust (push, security keys/U2F, OTP, SMS, hardware tokens, self-enrolment), device trust (device dashboard, health, BYOD vs corporate), adaptive policies (network, location, user group, Tor blocking, anomalous access, MDM/endpoint-management gating), secure app access and SSO
HyID-only rows: connector for third-party fingerprint/face authentication and Accops' own fingerprint/face authentication
Where Duo Network Gateway gives internal web/SSH/cloud app access, HyID needs an additional HySecure gateway (Silver/Gold) or has HySecure included (Platinum)
HyID rows for RADIUS/LDAP proxy, local database/LDAP without Active Directory, and on-premise deployment with no user sync to a third-party cloud
Some mobile device-trust rows are marked 'MDM needed' on the HyID side
cards.brief: A small single-sheet Excel checklist (created March 2021, last saved March 2023) comparing Cisco Duo's four editions with HyID's three editions row by row. Cells are 'x' or 'no' (a few 'MDM needed', 'Custom checks' or 'Additional HySecure Gateway'). There is no narrative, scoring or pricing for HyID. In the extracted text empty cells collapse, so read the column position in the original sheet before quoting a specific row.
cards.use_for: A Duo displacement or head-to-head MFA deal: 'which HyID edition matches Duo Access/Beyond?', 'does HyID need a gateway for internal apps?', 'can HyID run fully on-premise without cloud user sync?'. Internal checklist to build a customer-facing table from, not a document to send.
cards.stale_risk: Created March 2021, last saved March 2023 (the '2021-01-01' prefix is the bulk-rename date). Duo's editions and prices have since changed (Duo now sells Essentials/Advantage/Premier), so the Duo columns are out of date. HyID edition contents may also have changed.
cards.internal_reason: Internal competitive checklist with a competitor's historical price points; no verified public URL.
cards.needs_human: Refresh the Duo side against Duo's current editions (Essentials/Advantage/Premier) and prices before anyone quotes it, and confirm HyID Silver/Gold/Platinum is still the edition naming.

cards.title: Accops (on Azure) vs AWS WorkSpaces: Feature Comparison Spreadsheet (2017)
cards.key_problem: A customer choosing a cloud desktop service asks what Accops running on Azure does that AWS WorkSpaces does not.
key_outcomes: About 60 Yes/No rows: Accops in Azure vs AWS WorkSpaces
Desktop types: Accops offers flexible machine sizes, shared hosted desktops, published apps and Linux desktops; WorkSpaces had four fixed configurations and dedicated desktops only
Authentication: Accops built-in 2FA, OTP and biometrics; WorkSpaces relied on on-premise RADIUS
Endpoint data controls (copy-paste, print-screen, internet control, one-way file transfer, stealth mode) marked Yes for Accops, No for WorkSpaces
Protocol row: RemoteFX (Accops) vs PCoIP (WorkSpaces), with 'up to 128 Kbps' bandwidth
Endpoints and peripherals: Windows XP, Linux and mobile browsers, printers, scanners, dot-matrix printers, USB tokens and biometric devices supported by Accops, mostly No for WorkSpaces
cards.brief: A one-sheet Excel comparison of Accops VDI hosted on Azure against AWS WorkSpaces, created and last saved in December 2017 and marked 'CONFIDENTIAL, Copyright 2017'. It covers machine configuration and desktop types, gateway and authentication, endpoint security controls, display protocol, endpoint hardware and operating systems, browsers and peripheral support.
cards.use_for: Background for an AWS WorkSpaces objection, mainly the endpoint-control and peripheral rows (dot-matrix printers, USB tokens, biometric devices, copy/print blocking) that still differentiate. For current pricing against WorkSpaces use the DaaS DIY/AMD deck or the 2022 Why DaaS battlecard instead.
cards.stale_risk: December 2017. Many AWS columns are no longer true (WorkSpaces now has more bundles, Linux, built-in MFA options, and WSP/DCV instead of only PCoIP); Windows XP and RemoteFX are obsolete. Do not send as-is.
cards.internal_reason: Marked CONFIDENTIAL; a 2017 competitor comparison that is largely out of date.
cards.needs_human: Nine-year-old AWS WorkSpaces claims: retire or rebuild. The 2022 'Why DaaS' battlecard (slide 22) is a newer Accops-vs-WorkSpaces feature table and should be the one reps use.

cards.title: Nutanix Frame vs Accops: VDI Feature Comparison Spreadsheet (Nov 2020)
cards.key_problem: Nutanix customers and partners comparing Frame with Accops need a quick list of what each supports.
key_outcomes: About 25 Yes/No rows in three sections: VDI management, platform support, security
Accops-only rows: shared hosted (multi-session) desktops, USB redirection, Linux endpoints, client-based access, session and process performance logs, user self-service, access to physical PCs
Platforms: both run on Nutanix AHV and on Azure/AWS/GCP; Frame on Nutanix Cloud, Accops on VMware ESX and Hyper-V; Frame control plane SaaS, Accops on-prem
Security: Accops built-in gateway, MFA, contextual access, copy protection, session recording and watermark; Frame relies on the customer's VPN and third-party MFA
DaaS row names Nutanix XiFrame vs 'Accops Virtual Office'
cards.brief: A one-sheet Excel comparison created and saved on 3 November 2020 (the '2021-01-01' prefix is a bulk rename), listing features of Nutanix Frame against Accops with Yes/No cells. Nothing beyond the table - no pricing, sources or narrative.
cards.use_for: Internal background when a Nutanix-led deal also has Frame on the table. Treat it as history: Accops now positions as Nutanix's VDI partner, and the 'Customer Deck SEA 1.0' says Frame has been discontinued - check that before using either claim.
cards.stale_risk: November 2020. Frame has changed hands and product names since (the 2026 SEA customer deck calls it discontinued); 'Accops Virtual Office' is an old DaaS name; the 'on-prem only' control plane line predates Accops' SaaS offers.
cards.internal_reason: Internal competitive table about a Nutanix product; Nutanix is now a partner, so it should not be shared.
cards.needs_human: Probably retire: Frame's status has changed and Accops now sells alongside Nutanix. If kept, check the 'Frame discontinued' claim and replace 'Accops Virtual Office' with the current DaaS name.

cards.title: Event Request Template and Event SOP (Internal Marketing Form): Proposal Fields, Success Metrics, CEO Approval, Partner-Event Responsibilities and KPIs
cards.key_problem: Sales and partner managers proposing an event need a standard way to request it, get it approved and agree who owns what, so marketing can plan and audit it.
key_outcomes: Request sheet rules: the proposer must get the CEO's approval first; the request's ageing starts only once it reaches marketing with that approval; brand audit is marketing's job, post-event tracking the proposer's

Request fields: event type, proposer, city, mode, date, focus verticals, objective, two short-term and two long-term success metrics, budget, success owner, CEO approval, and for partner events the partner name, category, minimum promised audience, partner FY target and last-FY revenue

Drop-down lists: event types (with / through / to partner, existing customers, sponsored, Accops-own, partner connect, partner acquisition), approval states, Indian cities plus UAE, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and North Africa, objectives (reconnect, reinforce, empower, new customer acquisition, thought leadership, brand visibility)

Metric options: attendees, decision-makers attended, 5/5 feedback ratings, booth visitors, net new opportunities, opportunity conversion %, partner orders in the FY, net new conversion, upsell, cross-sell

SOP tab (images): per-event-type planning and execution tables, e.g. 'With Partner Events': budget approval by the executive leadership team, date and venue by partner + partner manager, venue and collateral by the partner to Accops brand guidelines, partner must deliver the minimum committed audience, speaker is the regional business head or presales head, leadership attends only for high-value partners, post-event follow-up by the partner manager measured in MQLs, auditing by marketing
cards.brief: An internal Excel workbook (created August 2022, last saved September 2025) with an 'Event Request' form sheet, an 'SOP' sheet whose content is pasted slide images (an 'Event Request CHECKLIST' and per-event-type responsibility/KPI tables) and a lookup sheet feeding the drop-downs. The partner-target field is labelled for FY 22-23.
cards.use_for: Answering 'how do I propose an event / a partner event?' and 'who does what for a partner event?': fill the Event Request sheet, get CEO approval, send to marketing; the SOP tab lists responsibilities and KPIs. Internal process document, not collateral.
cards.stale_risk: Created August 2022; the partner-target column still says FY 22-23 although the file was re-saved in September 2025. The SOP is only in images, so SAM can quote it only from this card.
cards.internal_reason: Internal approval process and partner-event rules.
cards.needs_human: Is this still the live event-request process? Update the 'Partner Target for 22-23FY' column label, and consider typing the SOP tables as text so they are searchable. The request sheet holds one stray partial entry ('28 augt').

cards.title: 'Beyond the Perimeter: Secure & Seamless Access' - CIOKlub 1-Hour Event Deck (July 2025): Zero Trust (Human, Device, Intent), HyID, HySecure with Quantum-Safe Encryption, VDI Benefits, 2,000-PC TCO, Proxmox/DaaS Offers
cards.client: Anonymised install-base slide (3rd largest private bank, largest e-commerce company, largest insurer, Indian government IT team, a Japanese university, a nuclear power company, a global service provider, India's largest company); Chennai, North India, Japan and MEA customer logo slides
cards.client_actual: Japan reference slide names Kyoto University, Ibaraki Prefectural, Okayama University, DHC Corporation, Fukuoka City, Kansai University, Aomori Prefecture, NTT Data Hokkaido, Marubeni Information Systems, University of Fukui and other Japanese cities and companies
cards.key_problem: Hybrid work, smart endpoints, Windows 10 end-of-life and DPDP push CIOs to secure access without adding more point products, while the VMware/Citrix ownership changes raise licensing costs.
key_outcomes: Opening (slides 3-6): new work models, CIO/CISO problems, challenges by offering (VDI, VPN, MFA, thin clients), 'what has changed since 2021' - Broadcom/VMware sale to Omnissa (KKR), Citrix PE buyout, bigger bundles and minimum licence purchases

Credentials (7-24): 1000+ customers, 200+ partners, 350+ team, 2M+ users; slide 7 says '2023 & 2024 Gartner MQ' while slide 8 says recognised in the 2025 DaaS MQ; DSCI Security Product Company of the Year 2024; HyDesk spec table and JioBook at INR 15,000; largest-customers slide; Chennai, North India, Japan and MEA reference slides

Zero trust (25-40): authenticate, validate human, device and intent, monitor (impossible travel, geo-location); HyID contextual/biometric/password-less MFA and SSO; vendor non-AD directory and desktop/server logon MFA case studies

ZTNA (41-50): VPN vs ZTNA, HySecure use cases, on-demand DLP, quantum threat (cites a CSO Online story on Chinese researchers and D-Wave), Kyber768/1024 and QRNG appliance support, Vajra secure enterprise browser

VDI (52-80): Windows 10 EOL, PC carbon footprint (Gartner 50% of IT GHG), VDI benefits and pros/cons, Digital Workspace on any hypervisor, shared desktops 50% cheaper than personal, 2,000-PC 5-year TCO (VDI Rs 27.21 crore vs desktops Rs 31.20 crore, 13% saving) with a full bill of quantities

Offers (82-90): Accops-supported Proxmox editions (Education Silver/Gold, Enterprise Gold/Platinum), 'DaaS in your datacenter' on Proxmox claimed 30% cheaper than Microsoft AVD, managed DaaS on Azure, NanoOS USB, HyMobile UEM, Reporting Server
Competitor grid (slide 91): Accops Digital Workspace vs Citrix, Omnissa, AVD, Zscaler/SASE and Okta/OneLogin/RSA; 'Why Accops' seven reasons
cards.brief: A 98-slide deck for a CIOKlub (Chennai CIO forum) session in July 2025, presented by Accops' co-founder, MD & CEO. Despite the '1Hour' name it is a full library: company credentials and reference customers, a zero-trust framework with HyID and HySecure, quantum-safe encryption, the VDI business case with a 2,000-PC TCO and BOQ, Proxmox and DaaS offers, other products, a competitor grid and a sustainability close. Several slides are image-only (demo video, reporting server screenshots, logo slides).
cards.use_for: A South India CIO audience in 2025: slide 18 is the Chennai customer logo slide, slide 79-80 the 2,000-PC TCO with BOQ, slides 48-49 the quantum-safe ZTNA story, slide 84 the Proxmox support editions, slide 91 the multi-vendor comparison grid. For 2026 events use the Sovereign CIO Conclave city decks instead.
cards.stale_risk: July 2025 (filename; last saved September 2025). Windows 10 EOL slide is now past. Gartner years conflict (slides 7 vs 8). The private bank's MFA users are 90,000 on slide 20 and 60,000 on slide 37. HyDesk country-of-origin row (UK, China, Thailand/Taiwan) sits beside 'Made in India'.
cards.internal_reason: Event deck with the CEO's personal digital identifiers on slide 29, install-base descriptors, internal pricing points and an unlicensed third-party image (Squarex).
cards.needs_human: Slide 29 ('Many Digital Identities') shows the CEO's real internal usernames, a bank customer ID and a personal email - replace with dummy values before this deck is shared. Reconcile 90,000 vs 60,000 MFA users and the Gartner years. Verify the D-Wave RSA-break slide and the 'Proxmox DaaS 30% cheaper than AVD' claim before reuse.

cards.title: Accops Partner Deck for a National Distributor's Event (20 Minutes, 3 June 2026): Credentials, Make-in-India Sovereignty, Six-Pillar Platform with Forcepoint SSE, Single-Vendor Case, June Offers, ACAP Certifications
cards.client: Prepared for a national IT distributor's partner session (named only in the filename); anonymised largest-customers slide
cards.key_problem: Channel partners need a short pitch of what Accops sells, why a Make-in-India single vendor, and what offers they can take to customers this month.
key_outcomes: Credentials (slides 2-4): 1000+ customers, 200+ partners, 350+ team, 2M+ users, part of Reliance since Sep 2023; About slide says '2023 & 2024 Gartner MQ' while slide 3 says recognised in the 2025 DaaS MQ; awards 2023-2025

Sovereignty (slides 5-7): 'Aligned with our PM's vision for Bharat' - Made-in-India ZTNA, data sovereignty, a slide listing a 7-point national call (WFH, buy Made-in-India and unrelated items such as gold buying, fuel, cooking oil, fertiliser, foreign travel); 'Time for preference bias for Make-in-India'

Largest-customers slide (8): same install-base descriptors as the 2026 decks (3rd largest private bank 10,000 VDI/ZTNA + 90,000 MFA, federal government IT 500,000 ZTNA, RBI for BYOD 350,000, largest company of India VDI 100,000, largest TPA in UK, 7th largest life insurer)

Single-vendor case (17-18): reduced licensing, no integration gaps, one support point; 'isolate your crown jewels, authorize each entry, restrict lateral movement'

Close: Why Accops (7 reasons) and ACAP partner certifications (IAM, VDI, ZTNA solution expert; certified sales professional)
